newsitem.title: UK: FLOOD IMPACT ON IRISH GRAINS SEEN LIMITED SO FAR.
newsitem.headline: FLOOD IMPACT ON IRISH GRAINS SEEN LIMITED SO FAR.

text.p: The flooding and heavy rain which has hit parts of Ireland may be a big problem for individual cereal growers, but so far the impact nationally looks likely to be limited, according to the Irish industry's association.
"I don't think it will affect the market," Seamus Funge, of the Cereals Association of Ireland, told Reuters by telephone from Dublin.
"It's unlikely the flooding will have any impact on the national tonnage," he said.
Winter barley had been harvested, but no wheat or spring crops so far.
Funge forecast the Irish cereals crop at around two million tonnes, a fall of around 130,000 tonnes on 1996's bumper level.

Some 307,000 hectares had been planted to grain, up on 1996 and the first time Irish plantings had exceeded 300,000 in the 1990s, Funge said. But yields would fall short of the record levels seen last year.
"What the crops need now is sun, sun and more sun. We're getting the opposite," he said.
But it was too early for the rain to have a major impact. "It depends on what happens from now to the end of August," Funge said.
